claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled "SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi" exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/
AWS CDK ties infrastructure to AWS only (AWS-only, no multi-cloud support), while Pulumi supports AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-prem.
AWS CDK allows developers to define infrastructure using only TypeScript or Python.
Pulumi supports any programming language; the CTA lists TypeScript, Python, Go, or C#.
CDK and CloudFormation generate an intermediary format (YAML or JSON) that is then executed to deploy resources.
Pulumi deployments are faster than AWS CDK because CloudFormation is slower than Pulumi's direct execution.
AWS CDK uses a CloudFormation state file while Pulumi uses Pulumi-managed state.
AWS CDK supports only AWS Secrets Manager for secrets management, whereas Pulumi offers cross-cloud secret support.
Pulumi provides real-time debugging.

A Founding Engineer at SST said: "With Pulumi, the deployment process feels like a natural extension of writing code - it's intuitive and powerful and capable of advanced things that traditional IaC tools can't handle."
Pulumi has built-in extensibility features such as custom providers and dynamic components.
Pulumi Insights product page provides improved visibility and debugging capabilities.
Pulumi Cloud Deployments supports advanced deployment workflows.
Ion is the code name for SST's new deployment engine that deploys components using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation, and once stable it will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
Pulumi Crosswalk for AWS exists and an AWS guide is at /docs/iac/guides/clouds/aws/.
SST's team expanded beyond AWS to other cloud providers and on-premises infrastructure, finding CDK's AWS-centric nature limiting.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account or Pulumi Cloud; the engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps its state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account rather than Pulumi Cloud.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, for deploying to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST apps are defined in a single sst.config.ts file using SST components.
Through 2023 SST's provisioning layer was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation.
In late 2023 the SST team began a rewrite code-named Ion, which shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's 'Moving away from CDK' blog post says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN).'

SST's 'Moving away from CDK' blog post says: 'When you run `sst deploy`, those resources make a call to an embedded Pulumi engine that makes a call to their bridged Terraform provider, and this makes the AWS SDK calls to create your resources.'
SST docs 'What is SST' say: 'SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi.'
Gautier Blandin's article says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says: 'You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now.'

SST's platform package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds, and others, and the Pulumiverse Vercel provider (@pulumi/aws, cloudflare, command, docker-build, random, tls, @pulumiverse/vercel).
The SST repository is now at anomalyco/sst (formerly sst/sst).
Pulumi's Terraform bridge is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, a network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API works for embedding Pulumi programs inside other tools.
Pulumi's provider bridge lets any Pulumi user consume Terraform providers directly.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Nitric docs state 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments', with official Nitric providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`; Defang deploys Docker Compose applications to the cloud.
Nitric is a cloud-agnostic application framework.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed as part of the same SST app.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The sst npm package gets roughly 796,000 downloads per week (796,291 for September 5-11, 2026).
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode has a larger GitHub following than SST itself.
SST doesn't invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
Pulumi Cloud, policy as code, and components offer cross-team visibility, central guardrails, and shared infrastructure patterns.
Pulumi's engine handles dependency resolution, preview and diff, and state tracking in SST.
